column1: Which Azure service can host DAB with request-based scaling and zero idle replicas?
column2:
Azure Container Apps.
Azure Container Apps can add replicas as HTTP demand increases. If the minimum is zero, it can also stop all replicas while idle. The first request can then wait for startup.
Review source

column1: Which Azure App Service feature lets you test a DAB release at a separate URL before swapping it into production?
column2:
Deployment slots.
A slot runs a separate copy of the app so you can test the release before swapping it into production. Basic plans do not support slots.
Review source

column1: You deploy the generic DAB container image. What application-specific files and settings must you give it?
column2:
Your DAB configuration and securely supplied runtime connection settings.
The engine image contains the server, not your entity mappings. Supply the JSON configuration and inject connection settings at runtime so the image does not carry a database password.
Review source

column1: What does managed identity remove from DAB's Azure SQL authentication?
column2:
The need to store a database password.
The host can get a Microsoft Entra token as its managed identity. DAB uses that identity to connect instead of storing a SQL login password. SQL permissions still apply.
Review source

column1: DAB can sign in to Azure SQL with managed identity. What must you configure inside the database to allow access?
column2:
A database user for the identity with the required SQL permissions.
Enabling the identity only makes it available to the host. Create a database user for it and grant the access DAB needs, such as SELECT on a table exposed for reads.
Review source

column1: App Service resolves a Key Vault reference as its managed identity. What access does that identity need in the vault?
column2:
Permission to read the referenced secrets.
App Service resolves the reference as the configured identity. Under Azure RBAC, Key Vault Secrets User is one way to grant the necessary secret access. Under access policies, grant Get.
Review source

column1: What happened to the built-in Database Connections feature in Azure Static Web Apps?
column2:
The feature retired on November 30, 2025.
The retired feature was the built-in Static Web Apps database integration, not DAB itself. You can still host DAB separately on Azure Container Apps or App Service.
Review source

column1: In a DAB release pipeline, what does Azure Container Registry store for the hosting service to pull?
column2:
It stores container images that the hosting service deploys.
The registry is where the pipeline publishes its container artifact and where the host pulls it. It stores the image but does not run the DAB service.
Review source

column1: Why tag a DAB container image with its source commit SHA?
column2:
To trace a deployed artifact to its source revision.
A source commit SHA is the identifier of the revision used to build the image. Including it in the tag lets you trace a running release back to that revision.
Review source

column1: A pipeline can push an image to Azure Container Registry. Why does it still need an Azure sign-in for Container Apps?
column2:
Registry access does not authenticate Azure resource-management operations.
Signing in to the registry authorizes image operations. Creating or updating a Container App also requires Azure resource access, usually established in the workflow with azure/login.
Review source

column1: DAB's root URL returns HTTP 200. Why does that not tell you whether it can connect to SQL?
column2:
The root endpoint returns basic service information without running database health checks.
The root response tells you that the API process answered HTTP. It can still answer while SQL is unavailable. Use a configured health check that tests the database dependency.
Review source

column1: DAB returns HTTP 403 from /health in production. What can this mean even when the database is healthy?
column2:
The probe is not authorized to read the health report.
DAB can reject a probe before it runs a database check. In production, omitting runtime.health.roles denies access to /health, so a 403 does not by itself diagnose a database failure.
Review source
